title: Research: fixed-port two-projection connector with 10 frame XORs
body:
## Result

This adds `research/two-projection-connector-seed51a5/`, an exact fixed-port construction for the universal five-source F2 connector. It keeps every inherited `B_j` and `A_m` child call at physical helper row `z0`, adds one arbitrary dirty helper row, and permits paid transitions among invertible two-row frames.

Use source word `[0,1,0,1,2,3,4,2,4,3]`. Sources 0, 1, 2 and 4 inject along logical direction `(1,0)`; source 3 injects along `(1,1)`. Readouts use covectors `(1,0)` and `(1,1)`. The corresponding prefix difference sets have sizes 26 and 16, and their union covers all 32 masks. `EXPECTED.json` gives one pair of readout boundaries for each of the 31 nonzero masks.

The complete-call lower bound in this interface is 10 source calls plus 62 output readouts, or 72 calls. The schedule meets it. The exact 945-by-32 word/direction census finds 175 covers using only these two projections. An exact six-frame dynamic program finds a 10-full-row-XOR schedule for the pinned readout pairs. This is not a minimization over alternative boundary-pair tables.

## Charged budget

The pinned one-row certificate prices `B0..B4` at `[1,4,10,16,28]` rank-one children and each output readout at one. The new schedule uses each B twice and each A twice, for 180 children. The current one-row `five_extra_output` schedule uses 10 B and 64 A calls for 182 children. Open PR #1770 reports 182 as the exact weighted optimum in the one-row alphabet.

The frame schedule adds 10 full-row XORs, or `10*L` bitwise XORs on length-L rows, and one extra length-L dirty helper. Independently conjugating each framed call would cost 28 row XORs; the global schedule reuses frames. If a rank-one child costs P(L) and a full-row XOR costs X(L), the local difference is `-2*P(L) + 10*X(L)`, plus the helper row. This is a conditional interface result; no finite-size runtime gain, selected-supplier occurrence, or new kappa is claimed.

## Scope and overlap

Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; accepted seed: `51a5e88d2c6fe1d9dc43f025b20473e1`; track `recursive-interfaces`, priority revision 3; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.

The accepted maintainer-reviewed conditional finite construction remains complex-binding at `836330098538459/500000000000000000`. Its review, source manifest and assembly certificate are pinned as provenance; none is changed.

A final cached overlap refresh covered 541 open PRs (fetched 2026-10-14T13:19:48Z) and 524 Discussion records (fetched 13:18:04Z), with complete pagination. Exact two-projection/fixed-port terms found no remote match; the cache warns live state may have changed. Immediately refreshed heads of nearby open work remain distinct: #1531 adds DUO and obtains 72 dispatches at 74 toggle-adds; #1770 optimizes the one-row weighted cost; #1812 obtains 72 calls with eight one-way transfers while allowing B/A calls to select either root. This PR keeps all B/A calls at physical `z0` and uses both paid shear directions in a persistent frame. The contracts differ, and no cost dominance over the port-selectable construction is claimed without a port-access and row-XOR tariff.

## Verification

- `python3 -I -O -B research/two-projection-connector-seed51a5/verify.py` — passes the 945-by-32 census, all 31 arbitrary-dirty output maps, helper restoration, shortest fixed-boundary frame schedule, 180-child invoice, and four negative controls.
- `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-projection-connector-seed51a5 --check-only` — `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`.
- CPython 3.14.7 was used locally. The registered runner requires Python 3.12, which is unavailable here; the Python 3.12 replay and repository-wide CI were not run. The selected-result reproduction was not rerun because the selected assembly is unchanged.
